warnings.why: Lesotho is famously known to have a very low share of arable land due to its mountainous terrain, usually reported around 10 percent rather than nearly 93 percent.
Turkmenistan is largely desert (Karakum Desert), and its agricultural land share is typically reported around 60 to 70 percent, making 84.3 percent an overestimate.

Saudi Arabia is predominantly arid desert with limited agricultural potential, traditionally reporting agricultural land shares around 70 to 80 percent primarily due to extensive low-productivity permanent pastures, making it border-line but highly dependent on how permanent pasture is classified.

Suriname is over 90 percent covered by tropical rainforest, so reporting only 0.473 percent agricultural land is plausible, but forestry and shifting cultivation definitions may distort comparability.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
